title: C1045 — Inline connector reading guide
introduction:
I read this inline connection as a handoff between harnesses. The face drawings provide the cavity addresses; the assignment table describes the circuits associated with them. Repeated addresses deserve attention: the table contains harness and engine variants, so the cavity number alone cannot tell the whole story.

Start with the MALE or FEMALE heading matching the harness you are researching, then use its identification table and drawing together. As drawn, the male face has the lower-numbered column on the left; the female face places it on the right. Follow the printed labels through the more closely spaced middle positions and the widely spaced end positions. Carry the cavity label across to the assignment table, then read Circuit Number, Color, Gauge, Function and Qualifier as a complete row.

A harness or engine qualifier narrows an entry's applicability. A blank qualifier leaves applicability unspecified, and repeated rows do not establish that every listed circuit is present together. The functions cover powertrain supplies, sensor signals, returns and grounds. Keep those descriptions distinct, including the literal fuse-or-circuit-breaker protection alternative. The identification table also records pigtail and shell information; those listings alone do not select a service part.

This guide supports reference reading. The drawings do not establish the physical viewing direction or how the housing projections operate. Size, Used and the gauge convention remain undefined here. Connector access, probing, test values and replacement work need the appropriate service procedure.

The summary Pin Count disagrees with the numbered positions in both drawings and the pigtail cavity count. That discrepancy remains unresolved and does not establish extra physical cavities.

edits.why: I start with the harness identity so the drawing and its adjacent identification row stay together. The printed labels establish positions within this drawing; the housing projections are landmarks, with no supported release movement assigned to them.

The column order reverses between the supplied drawings. Reading this face's own labels avoids carrying a left-or-right assumption across from the other face; the physical viewing direction still needs confirmation before any connector work.

Qualifier entries distinguish some harness and engine applications, while other alternatives remain unspecified. Circuit identifiers help distinguish similarly named signals, but this table alone cannot select among alternatives with overlapping or blank qualifiers. A signal return, a body ground and a power supply retain their separate recorded functions; none is a substitute test point for another.

Read each kit as a separate catalog entry with its own service part, engineering shell, gauge and material. The differing shell and gauge entries do not establish interchangeability or select a kit for a particular vehicle. These listings do not provide installation instructions.

originalAuthorHold: The identification table labels Pin Count as 49, while both supplied face drawings label cavities 1–16. The evidence does not define whether Pin Count counts assignment variants or conflicts with the illustrated connector. Clarify this before presenting it as a physical cavity total.

editorialRevision.scope: Complete independent active-agent review of all 80 primary units, four complete pages/two figures and four edits. Original first CLI author covered 61 units/three headings. Complete draft adds the pigtail heading and explicit count discrepancy, all table rows and raw text coverage. Original partial author retained separately; physical count and overlapping harness/engine alternatives remain unresolved for bounded source reading only.
